propositions.text: The principal claimant, spouse, and four children are Mexican citizens claiming refugee status under IRPA sections 96 and 97(1).
propositions.quote: The principal claimant, XXXXX XXXXX XXXXXX, his spouse, XXXXX XXXXX XXXXXX, and their four children, XXXX XXXX and XXXX XXXX, both minors, and XXXX XXXXX and XXXXX XXXXX XXXXXX, who are of the age of majority, are all citizens of Mexico. Mr. XXXXX XXXX and his family all allege that they are "Convention refugees" and "persons in need of protection" under section 96 and subsection 97(1) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act (IRPA).

paragraphs.summary: The court states the claimant family are Mexican citizens alleging refugee status under IRPA sections 96 and 97(1).

propositions.text: The father is the designated representative for his two minor sons.
propositions.quote: The father, XXXXX XXXXX XXXXXX, is the designated representative for his two minor sons, XXXX and XXXX.

paragraphs.summary: The court states the father is the designated representative for his two minor sons.

propositions.text: The principal claimant alleges he was threatened in Mexico City by unknown individuals dealing drugs on his street.
propositions.quote: The principal claimant alleged that he was XXXXXXXX Mexico City. He had a variety of problems because of individuals whose names he does not know who were dealing drugs on his street.

propositions.text: He knows the drug dealers' nicknames but does not have a good relationship with these neighbours.
propositions.quote: He knows their nicknames, XX XXXX and XX XXXX, but does not have a good relationship with these neighbours.

paragraphs.summary: The applicant alleges drug dealers threatened him in Mexico City and he knows their nicknames but has a poor relationship with them.

propositions.text: On a day in 2008, claimant found drug dealers selling drugs in front of his house and asked them to leave but they refused.
propositions.quote: He returned from work on XXXX, 2008, and found these people selling drugs in front of his house. He asked them to leave, but they did not cooperate.

propositions.text: A fist fight ensued after voices were raised, but neighbours and children intervened and made the dealers leave.
propositions.quote: Voices were raised and a fist fight ensued, but neighbours and the children arrived and made them leave.

paragraphs.summary: The applicant says he found drug dealers selling drugs near his home, asked them to leave, a fight occurred, and neighbours made them leave.

propositions.text: He did not file a complaint due to threats from the dealers and a neighbour's disappearance and death linked to them.
propositions.quote: He did not file a complaint against them because they often threatened people in the neighbourhood. Furthermore, a neighbour, XXXX, had problems with them and he disappeared in XXXX 2007. He was found dead one month later.

paragraphs.summary: The applicant alleges he did not complain because of threats and a neighbour's disappearance and death linked to the dealers.

propositions.text: The claimant and his parents confronted the dealers who refused to behave and threatened to kill them if complaints were filed.
propositions.quote: The next day, XXXX, 2008, the claimant and his parents went to see them to ask them to behave responsibly. The two individuals refused and threatened to kill them if they filed a complaint.

paragraphs.summary: The applicant says he and his parents confronted the dealers who threatened to kill them if complaints were filed.

propositions.text: On a night in 2008, the dealers blocked the claimant's driveway, argued, and one fired shots at him and his son as he fled.
propositions.quote: At about 10:30 p.m. on XXXX, 2008, the situation became more dangerous. The claimant returned from work XXXXXX and they blocked the driveway. They started arguing again. One hour later, one of them rang his doorbell and asked him to step outside. The claimant refused, and the man told him that they were fed up with him and they were going to kill him because he was interfering with their business. The claimant and his son XXXX tried to restrain him, but the man broke loose and ran toward the street. They were unable to catch him because he climbed into a XXXX XXXXXX and fired some shots at them as he left. They were not hit.

paragraphs.summary: The applicant recounts a night when dealers blocked his driveway, argued, and fired shots at him and his son as they fled.

propositions.text: They did not file a complaint because they feared the dealers and believed police cooperated with them.
propositions.quote: They did not file a complaint because they were scared and they knew that the police cooperates with them, because they are their clients and they receive payments to let them continue.

paragraphs.summary: The applicant alleges they did not complain due to fear and police cooperation with the dealers.

propositions.text: They decided to leave the country on a date in 2008.
propositions.quote: They therefore decided to leave the country on XXXX, 2008.

paragraphs.summary: The applicant states they decided to leave the country in 2008.

propositions.text: The panel finds the claimants are not Convention refugees or persons in need of protection after analyzing evidence.
propositions.quote: After analyzing the documentary and testimonial evidence, the panel is of the opinion that the claimants are not "Convention refugees" or "persons in need of protection."

paragraphs.summary: The court concludes the claimants are not Convention refugees or persons in need of protection after evidence analysis.

propositions.text: The panel is satisfied as to the identity of four claimants based on passport photocopies valid 2008-2011.
propositions.quote: In light of the documents submitted as evidence for XXXXX XXXXX XXXXXX, XXXXX XXXXX XXXXXX, XXXX XXXXX and XXXXX XXXXX XXXXXX, namely photocopies of the four passports, valid from XXXX, 2008, to XXXX, 2011, the panel is satisfied as to the identity of these four claimants.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the identity of four claimants established by passport photocopies valid 2008-2011.

propositions.text: The panel is satisfied as to the identity of two other claimants based on passport photocopies valid 2008-2011.
propositions.quote: In addition, XXXX XXXXX submitted as evidence the photocopies of his passport, which is valid from XXXX, 2008, to XXXX, 2011, and XXXXX XXXXX XXXXXX submitted the photocopies of his passport, which is valid from XXXX, 2008, until XXXX, 2011. The panel is therefore satisfied as to the identity of these two claimants.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the identity of two other claimants established by passport photocopies valid 2008-2011.

propositions.text: The principal claimant is not credible due to omissions and major contradictions in his testimony.
propositions.quote: The principal claimant is not credible, because of omissions and major contradictions that appeared during his testimony.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the principal claimant not credible due to omissions and contradictions in testimony.

propositions.text: The claimant stated three incidents occurred on specific dates in 2008 and was asked to recount them.
propositions.quote: During his testimony, the claimant stated that three incidents occurred, specifically on XXXXX and XX, 2008, and on XXXX, 2008. So the panel asked him to recount what took place during those incidents.

paragraphs.summary: The court notes the claimant stated three incidents occurred in 2008 and was asked to recount them.

propositions.text: Claimant said drug dealers forced him out of his car and hit him on a date in 2008.
propositions.quote: The claimant stated that when he arrived home on XXXX, 2008, the two drug dealers that he fears, XX XXXX and XX XXXX, forced him out of his car and hit him.

propositions.text: Claimant explained dealers opened car, grabbed him, and brought him out after panel's question.
propositions.quote: Surprised, the panel asked how they made him get out of a car and he replied that they opened it, grabbed him and brought him out.

propositions.text: Claimant's narrative said he went to dealers to tell them to go elsewhere, not that he was forced out of a vehicle.
propositions.quote: The panel points out that he wrote in his narrative1 that, during this incident, he went to see them to tell them to go elsewhere to conduct their business.

propositions.text: Claimant said he drove towards dealers, then they got him out and hit him.
propositions.quote: The claimant then stated that he drove towards them and that they then got him out and hit him.

paragraphs.summary: The court recounts claimant's inconsistent testimony about being forced out of his car and his narrative about the incident.

propositions.text: The panel rejects claimant's explanation because his narrative describes a fist fight outside, not involving a vehicle.
propositions.quote: The panel does not accept this explanation, because the claimant describes this event in two paragraphs2 and at no time is it mentioned that the claimant got out of a vehicle that day.

propositions.text: The narrative implies the fight was outside, making a fist fight in a vehicle unlikely.
propositions.quote: He states, on the contrary, that they got into a fist fight, which implies that they certainly were not in a vehicle, but were outside, since it would be difficult to have a fist fight in a vehicle.

paragraphs.summary: The court rejects claimant's explanation, finding the narrative implies the fight was outside, not involving a vehicle.

propositions.text: The panel does not believe the incident on a date in 2008 occurred due to contradictory descriptions undermining credibility.
propositions.quote: The panel does not believe that the incident of XXXXX took place, since he contradicted himself in describing the circumstances-that he was in a vehicle and that he was walking-and this undermines his credibility.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the incident did not occur due to contradictory descriptions undermining claimant's credibility.

propositions.text: Claimant said he and parents went to dealers' home to discuss and end the problem.
propositions.quote: The claimant recounted that, on the day after the incident of XXXXX, 2008, he and his parents went to see these two men at their home. He explained that it was in the hopes of having a discussion, of putting an end to this problem.

propositions.text: Dealers insulted them and told them not to file a complaint.
propositions.quote: However, instead of talking, they insulted them and told them not to file a complaint.

propositions.text: Claimant said dealers swore loudly at them when asked how insulted.
propositions.quote: A little later, the panel asked him how he had been insulted and he explained that they swore at them loudly.

propositions.text: Claimant initially said no death threats on that day but narrative states he received death threats.
propositions.quote: On that topic, the panel asked whether, on XXXXX, these men had said anything else to him, and he replied [translation] "not that I remember" and added that he did not remember. The panel noted that it is stated in his narrative that he received death threats on that day,3 and the claimant stated emphatically that he did not receive death threats, which surprised the panel.

propositions.text: Claimant said threats were against him, then corrected to say threats were against family.
propositions.quote: The panel pointed out that he also mentions in his narrative that a member of the family would pay very dearly for it. The claimant stated that no, the threats were against him. He added, as if to correct himself, that, if there were threats, they were against him; and that if there were death threats, it would be the same as making them against the family.

paragraphs.summary: The court recounts claimant's inconsistent testimony about visiting dealers, insults, and death threats.

propositions.text: After a break, claimant said he might have misunderstood question about death threats.
propositions.quote: Later, after a break, counsel again questioned the claimant on this topic, implying that the claimant first stated that he had received such threats and then stated that he had not. The claimant then explained that he might have misunderstood the question at that point.

paragraphs.summary: The court notes claimant said he might have misunderstood the question about death threats after a break.

propositions.text: The panel does not believe claimant went to dealers' home with parents due to unclear reasons and risk to parents.
propositions.quote: The panel does not believe that the claimant went to the home of these two drug dealers, first of all, because his reasons for doing so are not very clear and, secondly, because he alleged that he went there with his parents, including his mother.

propositions.text: Claimant said parents accompanied him to have a discussion.
propositions.quote: The panel asked him why he went with his parents and he replied that it was to have a discussion.

propositions.text: Panel finds parents unlikely to accompany claimant due to risk and no mention in narrative.
propositions.quote: The panel does not believe that they accompanied him because this would be putting them at risk, and more importantly, because he does not mention in his narrative that they accompanied him.

propositions.text: Claimant contradicted himself about receiving threats and tried to adjust testimony after break.
propositions.quote: Moreover, the claimant clearly stated that he did not receive such threats and then he tried to adjust his testimony after the break, when he was questioned by his counsel.

propositions.text: Claimant said he did not understand question but had repeated and acknowledged threats were against him.
propositions.quote: He then alleged that he had not understood the question, when, in fact, the claimant had repeated the sentence and stated that the threats were against him, which implies that he was well aware that they were talking about threats.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds claimant's testimony about visiting dealers with parents and threats is not credible and inconsistent.

propositions.text: The panel does not believe the incident of XXXXX took place, undermining the claimant's credibility.
propositions.quote: the panel does not believe that the incident of XXXXX took place, which undermines his credibility.

paragraphs.summary: The panel finds the incident of XXXXX did not occur, undermining the claimant's credibility.

propositions.text: There is a contradiction between the claimant's and his son's statements about the incident of XXXXX.
propositions.quote: there is a contradiction between the principal claimant's statement and that of his eldest son XXXXX.

propositions.text: The father said one man rang the doorbell; the son initially said two men came to the house.
propositions.quote: the claimant replied that he was and that he came right up to the house... XXXXX explained that, initially, there was one man and that later there were two men.

paragraphs.summary: The panel notes contradictory statements from the claimant and his son about the number of men at the door during the incident of XXXXX.

propositions.text: The panel rejects the son's explanation about the number of men, finding a contradiction and undermining his credibility.
propositions.quote: the panel is of the opinion that there is a contradiction between the father's contention that one person rang their doorbell and the son's statement that two people came to his house... This undermines his credibility.

paragraphs.summary: The panel finds the son's explanation contradictory and undermines his credibility regarding the incident of XXXXX.

propositions.text: The contradiction between father and son undermines their credibility and the panel does not believe the incident of XXXXX took place.
propositions.quote: This contradiction between the statements made by the father and those made by the son undermines their credibility and, consequently, the panel does not believe that the incident of XXXXX took place.

paragraphs.summary: The panel finds the contradictory statements undermine credibility and disbelieves the incident of XXXXX occurred.

propositions.text: Due to omissions and contradictions, the panel does not believe the events of XXXXX and XX and of XXXXX took place, nor that claimants were threatened by drug dealers.
propositions.quote: Because of these omissions and contradictions, the panel does not believe that the events of XXXXX and XX and of XXXXX took place and, consequently, the panel does not believe that the claimants were threatened by drug dealers as alleged.

paragraphs.summary: The panel disbelieves the events and threats by drug dealers due to omissions and contradictions.

propositions.text: The principal claimant's brother was murdered in 2010, two years after their departure in 2008.
propositions.quote: The principal claimant's brother, XXXX, was murdered on XXXX, 2010, almost two years after their departure on XXXX, 2008.

propositions.text: The panel believes the brother is deceased despite some exhibit errors.
propositions.quote: the panel believes that the claimant's brother, XXXX XXXXX XXXXXX, is deceased, even though some of the exhibits contain errors

paragraphs.summary: The panel finds the claimant's brother was murdered in 2010 and is deceased despite some exhibit errors.

propositions.text: The claimant alleges his brother was murdered by a neighbour due to gang-related vengeance.
propositions.quote: The principal claimant alleged that this brother died because someone living across the street... killed XXXX out of vengeance... because he and XXXX had had a number of problems with drug dealers.

propositions.text: The claimant's mother gave a police statement explaining the murder was due to a dispute involving a gang member named XXXXX.
propositions.quote: In her statement to the police, she explains that her son was killed because of a disagreement... with a man named XXXXX... who was a member of a gang.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant alleges his brother was murdered by a neighbour over gang disputes, supported by the mother's police statement.

propositions.text: The claimant's mother stated the brother had a police record and served time in penitentiary.
propositions.quote: in her statement to the police, his mother states that his brother XXXX had a police record for theft and that he served time in a penitentiary.

propositions.text: The claimant downplayed the brother's incarceration and avoided discussing it further.
propositions.quote: The claimant tried to play down that fact... The claimant clearly did not want to discuss it any further.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant downplayed his brother's incarceration despite the mother's statement, avoiding further discussion.

propositions.text: The panel doubts the mother's explanation for the brother's murder as it seems unlikely someone would be killed for a minor reason.
propositions.quote: the panel has difficulty believing that someone could be killed for such a minor reason.

propositions.text: The brother lived near the claimant in an unsafe neighbourhood described as 'dark and dangerous'.
propositions.quote: the claimant stated at the hearing that his brother XXXX lived near him... the newspaper describes the streets... as 'dark and dangerous neighbourhood streets'

paragraphs.summary: The panel doubts the mother's minor-reason explanation for the brother's murder in an unsafe neighbourhood.

propositions.text: The panel believes the brother's murder was a settling of accounts related to organized crime, not a neighbour dispute.
propositions.quote: the panel is of the opinion that the mother's story... is rather far-fetched... it was actually a settling of accounts related to organized crime.

propositions.text: The murder occurred two years after claimant's departure and the claimant only mentioned problems with drug dealers shortly before the hearing.
propositions.quote: this murder took place almost two years after the claimant's departure... he only mentions it in the exhibit submitted on February 3, 2011... 'My brother and I had many problems with drug dealers...'.

propositions.text: The claimant's reluctance to explain the brother's incarceration surprised the panel.
propositions.quote: His reluctance surprised the panel.

propositions.text: Counsel argued 'settling of accounts' is vague and could indicate neighbourhood or organized crime problems.
propositions.quote: Counsel later alleged that the expression 'settling of accounts' is a very vague expression that could indicate a problem in the neighbourhood just as well as problem with organized crime.

propositions.text: The panel finds the newspaper's use of 'settling of accounts' indicates organized crime involvement.
propositions.quote: the panel is of the opinion that the use of this expression in a newspaper article... indicates that it is very unlikely that this was simply a dispute between neighbours, but that it was actually a settling of accounts related to organized crime.

paragraphs.summary: The panel finds the brother's murder was likely organized crime settling of accounts, rejecting counsel's vague argument.

propositions.text: The panel asked about links between the brother's death and men who attacked the claimant; the claimant struggled to show connections.
propositions.quote: the panel asked him about the connection... The claimant was hard pressed to demonstrate that there might be links...

paragraphs.summary: The claimant struggled to demonstrate links between his brother's death and men who attacked him.

propositions.text: The claimant gave inconsistent explanations about connections between the killer and drug dealers.
propositions.quote: The claimant offered a variety of explanations in response to the panel's questions on this subject.

propositions.text: The panel found the claimant's explanations strange and inconsistent, including about his mother's knowledge and complaint.
propositions.quote: The panel pointed out that it is strange that his mother did not mention any names... The claimant stated that it was to protect herself... The panel pointed out that she had already named XXXXX... He replied that it was indeed because she was scared.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant gave inconsistent and strange explanations about connections between the killer and drug dealers.

propositions.text: The panel believes the claimant is adjusting facts to fit his story and does not believe a connection exists between the brother's death and drug dealers.
propositions.quote: The panel is of the opinion that the claimant is trying to adjust the new facts... The panel does not believe that there is a connection between his brother XXXXX death and the two drug dealers...

paragraphs.summary: The panel finds the claimant adjusts facts and disbelieves a connection between the brother's death and drug dealers.

propositions.text: The panel finds the murder unrelated to the claimant's or mother's alleged motives and that the claimant used the death to support his story, undermining credibility.
propositions.quote: the panel is of the opinion that this murder is in no way connected to the motives alleged... The panel is of the opinion... that the claimant used this death to support his own story. This undermines his credibility.

paragraphs.summary: The panel finds the murder unrelated to alleged motives and that the claimant used it to support his story, undermining credibility.

propositions.text: The panel concludes the claimants are not credible.
propositions.quote: For all these reasons, the panel is of the opinion that the claimants are not credible.

paragraphs.summary: The panel concludes the claimants lack credibility.

propositions.text: The panel concludes claimants did not establish a serious possibility of persecution or risk of torture, death, or cruel treatment if returned to Mexico.
propositions.quote: the panel concludes that the claimants did not establish that they face a 'serious possibility' of persecution on one of the Convention grounds... or a risk to their lives or to a risk of cruel and unusual treatment or punishment, should they return to Mexico.

paragraphs.summary: The panel concludes claimants failed to prove serious risk of persecution or harm if returned to Mexico.

propositions.text: The panel rejects the claimants' refugee protection claims.
propositions.quote: their claims for refugee protection are rejected.

paragraphs.summary: The panel rejects the claimants' refugee protection claims.
